subject.title: Codex real fork corpus: 5,427 replayed parent events across rewritten timestamps

question: Is this corpus report sufficient to begin the canonical cross-file provenance design, or should the reporter first provide the offered numeric fixture and instrumented current-main initial and cached repeat-scan output?
rationale: The merged containment work explicitly deferred affected real-setup validation, while the remaining implementation changes ownership and cache semantics that should not be chosen from token-value similarity alone.

options.title: Request fixture and scan proof
options.body: Ask for the numeric-only fixture plus redacted current-main initial and repeat-scan summaries before approving the family-ledger design.

options.title: Accept the report as sufficient
options.body: Treat the documented 5,427-event match as adequate proof and move architectural discussion to the canonical issue immediately.

recommendation.title: Request fixture and scan proof
recommendation.body: Ask for the numeric-only fixture plus redacted current-main initial and repeat-scan summaries before approving the family-ledger design.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository-level approval is appropriate because the remaining work introduces broad cross-file ownership and cache behavior.
